question: What metal toxicity was frequently documented by physicians in ancient civilizations?
explanation: Ancient writers and physicians observed severe colic and paralysis among workers exposed to lead in mines and painting. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why did ancient laborers suffer greatly from occupational hazards without intervention?

options.A: Laborers lacked legal protections and basic medical care
options.B: Physicians lacked any interest in treating lower-class citizens
options.C: Ancient rulers mandated dangerous work to test human limits
options.D: Workers refused to wear protective equipment made of leather

explanation: Enslaved persons and poor artisans faced severe workplace dangers because society offered no legal safeguards or healthcare for them. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h1)

question: The Industrial Revolution caused a massive rise in workplace injuries primarily due to what factor?

options.A: Extreme outdoor weather conditions inside the factories
options.B: Workers refusing to follow basic hygiene instructions
options.C: A sudden shortage of trained medical personnel
options.D: Fast-moving machinery without adequate safety guards

explanation: Mechanization introduced heavy, unguarded industrial equipment that frequently caused severe trauma and crushing injuries. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h2)

question: A factory worker from the nineteenth century presents with severe bone decay in the jaw after working in a matchstick plant. This condition is caused by exposure to which substance?
explanation: Phossy jaw was a classic occupational disease caused by chronic exposure to white phosphorus in match manufacturing. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h2)

question: Who is widely recognized as the father of occupational medicine?
explanation: Bernardino Ramazzini wrote the foundational text linking specific jobs to specific illnesses in the early eighteenth century. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h3)

question: Why did Bernardino Ramazzini introduce a specific question about a patient's job into medical evaluations?

options.A: To help hospital administrators bill the correct employer for care
options.B: To connect daily workplace exposures directly to presenting symptoms
options.C: To determine the social status and income of the sick person
options.D: To evaluate whether the worker could afford expensive medicines

explanation: Understanding a patient's daily trade allows clinicians to identify toxic exposures and repetitive strains causing their illness. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h3)

question: Early legislative acts during the industrial era primarily focused on protecting which vulnerable group?
explanation: Initial labor laws targeted the extreme exploitation and long working hours imposed on young children in factories. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h4)

question: How did the role of government change regarding factory safety after the passage of early labor laws?

options.A: Safety became a regulated public health priority rather than private business
options.B: Factory inspectors were banned from entering private manufacturing floors
options.C: Governments took over direct ownership of all hazardous industrial plants
options.D: Employers gained total freedom to set their own internal safety rules

explanation: Legislation established that the state has a duty to enforce minimum safety standards and protect workers from abuse. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h4)

question: What was a primary responsibility of the earliest industrial nurses in manufacturing settings?

options.A: Managing corporate finances and payroll distribution
options.B: Designing safer factory machinery and ventilation systems
options.C: Enforcing strict disciplinary rules for lazy workers
options.D: Treating acute injuries and promoting basic sanitation

explanation: Early occupational health nurses provided immediate first aid and worked to improve hygiene to prevent widespread infections. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h5)

question: Why did the presence of on-site nurses benefit early industrial employers?

options.A: It eliminated the need for any future safety legislation
options.B: It allowed factories to increase operating speeds safely
options.C: It completely stopped all machinery-related accidents
options.D: It reduced worker absenteeism and lowered infection rates

explanation: Prompt medical attention kept workers healthier, reducing time lost from work and stabilizing factory productivity. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h5)

question: Which international body was established in 1919 to create global standards for fair labor?
explanation: The International Labour Organization was founded to unify international efforts in establishing safe and fair working conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary function of global health organizations regarding occupational safety in developing nations?

options.A: Directly managing factory floors in developing member countries
options.B: Purchasing protective equipment for every private corporation
options.C: Financing all worker compensation claims across the globe
options.D: Providing guidelines to build robust industrial health infrastructures

explanation: Global agencies establish standards and offer expert frameworks to help countries protect workers as they industrialize. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h6)

question: How has the focus of occupational health nursing shifted in modern work environments?

options.A: From factory prevention to purely administrative corporate management
options.B: From international standards to strictly local workplace rules
options.C: From physical injuries alone to include mental health and chronic stress
options.D: From treating acute trauma to ignoring office-based employees

explanation: Modern workplaces require nurses to manage psychological well-being, burnout, and ergonomic strain alongside physical safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h7)

question: A nurse designs an outreach program for informal market workers in Nigeria who lack formal factory safety regulations. Which approach is most effective for this group?

options.A: Providing practical preventive education and localized safety awareness
options.B: Focusing solely on desk ergonomics and computer screen glare
options.C: Waiting until the government passes strict international factory laws
options.D: Fining local vendors who fail to wear heavy industrial boots

explanation: Informal sectors require community-based education and accessible health guidance since standard corporate regulations do not apply. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h7)
